gaps.what: 1832-1833 (State then Republic of New Granada) is covered by no Cliopatria row; republic-of-new-granada (row from 1834) needs a new keyframe
Carabobo, Pichincha and the annexation of Guayaquil are undated on the opened pages (confidence 1-2); the 1819-1820 land held is a bridge from Cliopatria's New Granada 1820 shape
Proclamation of Agustin I and the date Chiapas joined are not on the opened pages; Chiapas is confidence 1
El Salvador stayed in the federation until 30 January 1841 (no event: the dossier ends April 1839); Los Altos (1838-1839) and Guanacaste not dated

The 1825 loss of 1,217 Brazilian-Amazon cells to Cliopatria's Bolivia shape, the 1853 loss of 29 Brazilian cells, Tarata (1926) and the 1950 one-cell blip are not explained by any opened page; what San Martin held in 1822-1824 is not on the pages
Tacna, Arica and the other Chilean-occupied departments (1880-1929) are kept inside Peru's shapes with occupation events; republic-of-chile must mirror them or the two dossiers disagree

Not opened: Reform War (1857-1860), Yucatan's secessions (1841-1843, 1846-1848), Caste War, Zacatecas rebellion (1835), Soconusco's 1842 annexation (no month); 1842 transfer of the north to Centralist Mexico is Cliopatria-based (confidence 1)
Second Mexican Empire / Mexican Monarchists rows (1864-1867) claim the cells that this dossier keeps Mexican with hatched occupations; the three dossiers must use one reading

counterparts_needing_dossiers.name: Central America (Act of Independence), the independent provinces of the Captaincy General of Guatemala

problems: Cliopatria's Federated Republic of Mexico row is a regime (1824-1835, 1846-1865) plus a northern remnant in 1836-1845, parallel to the Centralist Mexico row (another group, Wikidata Q5062192 shared with 'Mexico'); the dossier ends 1867-06 (Republic restored) instead of 1865 and keeps Mexico sovereign under hatched French and Imperial occupations; the second-mexican-empire, mexican-monarchists, centralist-mexico and mexico dossiers must be reconciled with it, and the colour agent should give them one family hue.

Cliopatria draws Tacna, Arica, Moquegua and parts of Puno, Lima and Ica as Chilean 1880-1925; the Peru dossier keeps them Peruvian with occupation events (the Treaty of Ancon gave Chile only temporary control of Tacna and Arica); republic-of-chile must mirror them.

Cliopatria's Gran Colombia 1824-1829 shape includes Bolivia, 59 percent of Paraguay and part of Chile (wrong); the 1830-1833 shape keeps Venezuela and Ecuador after 1830. Gran Colombia ends 1831-11, leaving 1832-1833 to republic-of-new-granada.
Page budgets exceeded: gran-colombia 3 pages (budget 1-2); federated-republic-of-mexico 11 (budget 9, including the shared Soconusco page and a Baja California page for a counterpart event).
Several Wikipedia pages are thin (First Mexican Republic gives no area; Brazil-Peru border gives only 1909); affected events are confidence 1 or flagged in notes.
Counterpart string 'Central America (Act of Independence)' (used in first-mexican-empire, as in the Spanish Empire dossier) is not a slug.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_intervention_in_Mexico is a disambiguation page; Second_French_intervention_in_Mexico was opened instead.
